page.title: Credentials
page.purpose: Let an operator provision each credential the selected stack declares, knowing what it unlocks and where to get one, without the value ever being displayed or stored.

priorities.statement: An operator never faces an unexplained password box.
Getting a credential is one click away from needing it.
A value is never shown, echoed, or recoverable from this surface.
A host with no secure store is told how to create one, not that it failed.

states.description: One card per declared descriptor with its configured status.
A value is being relayed to the credential authority.
The authority rejected the value or was unreachable; the cause is named.
This host has no native secure store; the encrypted file store is offered as the path forward.

elements.description: The descriptor's declared purpose — what this credential unlocks.
The descriptor's obtain_url — where an operator signs up for or generates this value.
elements.name: Get one

elements.description: Write-only value entry; masked and never populated from a read.
Relays the value to the credential authority.
elements.name: Save securely

elements.description: Configured or unconfigured. Never a value.
Names the backend condition and its specific fix.
How to initialize the encrypted file store on a host with no session.

claims.statement: Every credential card states what the credential unlocks; no card is a bare password box.
Every credential whose descriptor declares an obtain URL offers a link to it.
No element on this page ever renders a credential value, in any state.
claims.rationale: The input exists only as a write path. A configured credential shows status, never a populated field.

claims.statement: Within a credential card, saving the value is the single dominant action.
A failed save names whether the value was rejected or the store was unreachable, and what to do next.
A host with no native store is shown how to create the encrypted store, not told that provisioning failed.
Credential entry and save are operable by keyboard alone.
